description: The 18 Elastic Defend GenAI prebuilt rules from elastic/detection-rules main at 29aaacb49, the Defend promotion rule, and PoC copies keyed on process.ai_agent.* where an original identifies agents by process name.

rules.name: Connection to Common Large Language Model Endpoints
rules.no_copy_reason: Doesn't identify agents. It looks for interpreters, script hosts and unsigned binaries resolving LLM API domains, so agents are what it's trying to tell apart from, not what it keys on.

rules.name: GenAI Process Connection to Suspicious Top Level Domain
GenAI Process Connection to Unusual Domain
Package Runtime Secret File Access Followed by IMDS Request
rules.no_copy_reason: Doesn't identify agents. It keys on package runtimes (python, node, ruby and so on) and package install paths, for supply chain malware.

rules.name: Claude Cowork VM Boot Image Tamper
rules.no_copy_reason: The agent list is an exclusion for the legitimate writer (the Claude desktop app). Swapping it for process.ai_agent.* would exclude any Claude-tagged process, including a Claude Code descendant doing the tampering, which inverts the rule. Whether Defend tags the desktop app at all is unknown.

rules.name: GenAI CLI Started with Unsafe Permission Bypass
Unusual Process Modifying GenAI Configuration File
rules.no_copy_reason: Doesn't identify agents. It keys on agent configuration file paths and a new process.executable, whoever writes them.

rules.name: GenAI Process Compiling or Generating Executables
GenAI Process Performing Encoding/Chunking Prior to Network Activity
Execution via OpenClaw Agent
rules.no_copy_reason: Specific to OpenClaw, found by node command line. We only know Defend's process.ai_agent.name values for Claude Code (claude_code) and Cursor (cursor). A generic 'any agent spawns a shell' copy would fire on every Claude Bash call.

rules.name: Potential Prompt Injection Coercing Shell Execution
rules.no_copy_reason: No agent list. It matches any shell whose parent command line has an injection phrase, so install method doesn't matter.

rules.name: Potential Destructive AWS CLI Command Executed by GenAI Agent
Elastic Defend Alerts from GenAI Utility or Descendant
GenAI Agent Instruction File Written to Downloads
rules.no_copy_reason: Doesn't identify agents. The process list is browsers and archive tools writing AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md into Downloads.

rules.name: Ollama API Accessed from External Network
rules.no_copy_reason: Ollama is a local model server, not a coding agent. Nothing suggests Defend tags it with process.ai_agent.*.

rules.name: Ollama DNS Query to Untrusted Domain
rules.no_copy_reason: Ollama is a local model server, not a coding agent. Nothing suggests Defend tags it with process.ai_agent.*.

rules.name: GenAI or MCP Server Child Process Execution
